correctness.rationale: The original mathematics is correct. For a positive ordered composition of h, every intermediate harmonic factor lies between H_{n-h} and H_{n-1}. The derivative of the logarithmic power series gives h b_{h,k}=k∑_{j<h}b_{j,k−1}; dropping the sum constraint yields kH_{h−1}^{k−1}, and the box of entries ≤h^{1−ε} gives the matching fixed-k asymptotic when ε decreases to zero. With a either endpoint reciprocal harmonic normalizer, aH_{h−1}→θ<1 gives a summable bound kq^{k−1} with q<1 on h a^{k−1}b_{h,k}, including zero terms beyond h. This yields the hit normalization and count masses, which sum to one. For the repaired central claim at each fixed k, the uniform multiplicative 1+o(1) comparison transfers the normalized composition law in total variation. Bounding all but the r-th decrement by h^{t_i}, t_i<1, forces the r-th to be h(1−o(1)); multiplying harmonic sums and dividing by b_{h,k} gives joint rectangular limiting mass (∏t_i)/k. Summing the disjoint events for all r and taking the cutoffs up to 1 proves the uniqueness of the giant with high probability, and the rectangles prove the joint index/logarithm law with coordinates in time order. The k=1 case is exact. The tagged-clade identity is consistent with n/(n−h)→1. No result at θ=1 or uniform in growing k is used or claimed. The supplied finite checker was inspected, not executed. Checked the prior-implication calculation now included in the repaired file: the factor after extracting (1−t) from the beta weight is H_{q−1}(n−1)/[h(q−1)], and O(1/h) exceptional probability is negligible relative to log⁻²(n/h).

Berg–Durán have ρ(t)=∑α_j t^{ξ_j}, j<ξ_j<j+1, α_j∼log⁻²j. Squeezing between neighboring integer powers and Abelian summation gives (1−t)ρ(t)∼log⁻²(1/(1−t)).
